t.6.100.1: Having witnessed the slaying of Rāvaṇa, those Devas, Gandharvas and Dānavas departed, each in his own aerial chariot, telling auspicious tales as they went.
t.6.100.2: The terrible slaying of Rāvaṇa, the valor of Rāghava, the splendid fighting of the monkeys, and the counsel of Sugrīva.
t.6.100.3: Speaking of the devotion and the valor of Lakṣmaṇa, son of Sumitrā, the illustrious ones departed in delight, going back the way they had come.
t.6.100.5: Permitted by Rāghava, Mātali, the charioteer of Śakra, mounted that divine chariot and ascended to heaven itself.
t.6.100.4: But the illustrious Rāghava, having given leave to the divine chariot bestowed by Indra, radiant as fire, paid honor to Mātali in return.
t.6.100.6: When that best of the charioteers of the gods had ascended to heaven, Rāghava, supremely delighted, embraced Sugrīva.
t.6.100.7: Having embraced Sugrīva and been respectfully saluted by Lakṣmaṇa, he came to the camp of the army, honored by the foremost of the monkeys.
t.6.100.8: And then Rāma spoke to Lakṣmaṇa, the son of Sumitrā, who stood close beside him, endowed with courage and blazing with splendor.
t.6.100.9: O gentle one, consecrate this Vibhīṣaṇa as king in Laṅkā, for he is attached to me, devoted to me, and has truly been my helper.
t.6.100.10: This is my supreme desire, gentle one: that I may see this Vibhīṣaṇa, the younger brother of Rāvaṇa, consecrated as king in Laṅkā.
t.6.100.11: Thus addressed by the great-souled Rāghava, Saumitri said, "So be it," and, delighted, took up a golden pitcher.
t.6.100.12: With that pitcher, Saumitri, at Rāma's command, consecrated Vibhīṣaṇa as king in Laṅkā, in the midst of the rākṣasas.
t.6.100.13: That righteous-souled one consecrated the pure-souled Vibhīṣaṇa. His ministers rejoiced, as did those rākṣasas who were devoted to him.
t.6.100.14: Seeing Vibhīṣaṇa consecrated in Laṅkā as lord of the rākṣasas, Rāghava, together with Lakṣmaṇa, attained the highest joy.
t.6.100.15: Having obtained that great kingdom given by Rāma, Vibhīṣaṇa reassured his subjects and then approached Rāma.
t.6.100.16: Then the night-roaming citizens, overjoyed, brought to him unbroken grains of rice, sweetmeats, parched grain, and heavenly flowers as well.
t.6.100.17: Taking them, that invincible and valorous one presented to Rāghava, and to Lakṣmaṇa as well, everything that was auspicious and propitious.
t.6.100.18: Seeing Vibhīṣaṇa with his task accomplished and his aims fulfilled, Rāma accepted all of that, solely out of a wish to please him.
t.6.100.19: Then Rāghava spoke these words to Hanūmān, the monkey, a hero like a mountain, who stood at his side with joined palms.
t.6.100.20: O gentle one, having obtained the permission of this great king Vibhīṣaṇa, and having entered the house of Rāvaṇa and approached with humility…
t.6.100.21: O best of victors, tell Vaidehī that I am well, together with Sugrīva and Lakṣmaṇa, and that Rāvaṇa has been slain by me.
t.6.100.22: O lord of the monkeys, having told Maithilī this pleasing news and received her message in return, you should come back.
